Amodei noted that slowing development was floated as early as twenty twenty-three. He said it was previously unnecessary because models lacked real-world action capabilities. They also lacked significant deception or cyberattack skills.
He believes slowing down could buy an extra year or two. This time will help advance model alignment and reduce catastrophic risks.

item.title: Japan's Hayabusa2 achieves first-ever laser ranging experiment with an asteroid
item.description: Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency successfully conducted the first laser ranging experiment with an asteroid. This happened during a flyby of Torifune on Sunday, July fifth. The milestone marks the first exploration target of the Hayabusa2 spacecraft's Extended Mission. The probe used its Lalt laser altimeter instrument to fire the laser twice during the flyby. The first fire occurred at six twenty-nine p.m. from a distance of about twenty kilometers. The second fire happened from a distance of fifteen kilometers. The spacecraft traveled at a speed of five point three kilometers per second. It targeted the asteroid with a narrow beam that struck surface areas measuring thirty meters and twenty-three meters. The Lalt instrument was originally developed from the altimeter used by J A X A.'s Kaguya lunar orbiter. It previously gathered topographical data on asteroid Ryugu. Laser ranging adds scale to spacecraft images. It helps determine the size, density, porosity, and surface reflectance of astronomical objects. When combined with tracking data, the technique accurately determines a celestial body's position. This improves orbital predictions. The capability advances future missions involving near-Earth asteroids. It also supports planetary defense by allowing scientists to predict potential collision risks. The mission team is currently analyzing data to determine the exact surface location where the laser struck.

item.title: Automattic confirms Mullenweg has returned as CEO after attempted ouster by board
item.description: Automattic has confirmed that WordPress founder Matt Mullenweg has returned as chief executive officer following an attempted ouster by the company board. The board had previously voted to put him on a paid leave of absence. TechCrunch reports that Automattic confirmed his removal on Wednesday, while Chief Financial Officer Mark Davies briefly served as interim chief executive officer during the leadership dispute. Following the surprise removal attempt, Mullenweg accused board members of conspiring against him. Board member and founding chief executive officer Toni Schneider reportedly stepped down and now leads Bluesky, though Schneider did not return requests for comment. An Automattic spokesperson stated via email to TechCrunch just after five p. m. Eastern Time on Saturday that Mullenweg holds the position of chairman and chief executive officer with the full support of the board and top executives. Automattic stated on Monday morning that Mullenweg was away for exactly thirty-three hours and twenty minutes. Mullenweg resisted the move by removing other administrators from the company Slack. He told employees he was back in control, posted messages declaring he was a pirate, used cursing, and wrote that if it was an human resources problem someone should wrangle him in. When asked if his comments were legitimate, he wrote a blog post about buying a houseboat and stated he was a pirate rather than a troll. He also noted on X that this was likely the fifth time he has faced a coup.

item.title: AI uncovers hidden Ozempic side effects across 400,000 Reddit posts
item.description: On September thirteenth, twenty twenty-six, researchers at the University of Pennsylvania School of Engineering and Applied Science published a study in Nature Health. Artificial intelligence analysis of more than four hundred thousand Reddit posts across five years uncovered overlooked symptoms. The posts came from users of G. L. P. one medications including Ozempic, Wegovy, Rybelsus, Mounjaro, and Zepbound. The study examined posts from nearly seventy thousand users of semaglutide and tirzepatide. Large language models enabled researchers to quickly process and categorize vast amounts of informal text. They used the Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities for the analysis. About forty-four percent of users described known gastrointestinal side effects. The A. I. also detected unprompted reports of fatigue and body temperature issues. These temperature issues included chills and hot flashes. Users also reported reproductive symptoms including menstrual irregularities. Nearly four percent of users who reported side effects described menstrual changes, a figure co-author Neil Sehgal notes would be even higher in a female-only sample. Researchers noted that the findings do not establish causation between the medications and the reported symptoms. Lead author Neil Sehgal notes that they cannot say the drugs are actually causing these symptoms. Co-author Lyle Ungar, who previously participated in a similar twenty eleven effort to identify adverse drug effects from internet material, notes that clinical trials can fail to find what symptoms patients are most concerned about. These drugs interact with the hypothalamus, which regulates hormones and body temperature. Because of this, the patterns may serve as valuable leads. Some side effects like nausea are well known, showing the method works. Underreported symptoms came directly from patients. Senior author Sharath Chandra Guntuku stated that these underreported symptoms are leads that clinicians could potentially pay attention to.

item.title: Arch Manning leads Texas back from 20 points down in fourth quarter to shock No 1 Ohio State
item.description:
Arch Manning led number four Texas back from a twenty-point fourth-quarter deficit to beat number one Ohio State twenty-four to twenty-three on Saturday night. This twenty-point comeback is the largest fourth-quarter rally to win against an Associated Press number one team, according to Sportradar.
The game started poorly for Texas as Manning committed early turnovers with a fumbled completion and a fluke interception that helped stake Ohio State to a ten to nothing lead. The Buckeyes extended their advantage to twenty-three to three in the third quarter before a sideline hit on Manning sparked the Longhorns offense. Manning finished the night completing twenty-three of thirty-seven passes for one hundred ninety-six yards and one touchdown, directing three scoring drives of twelve plays or longer. Hollywood Smothers secured two short touchdown runs, including the last one with just twenty-five seconds remaining.
Texas coach Steve Sarkisian praised his quarterback resilience following the win. His grit started it, Sarkisian said, adding that getting through the adversity of last season helped him get through the adversity of tonight. When he comes back, everybody else comes back. That is a guy who has some grit, some resilience. Manning finished the game reflecting on the response of his team, stating it was a weird start and noting he was really proud of the way they responded.

item.title: Russians on the Goethe-Institut: 'Hostage to politics'
item.description: Germany's Goethe-Institut is closing all of its Russian branches by Sunday, September thirteenth, twenty twenty-six. The Russian Foreign Ministry ordered the closure of the German cultural centers in Moscow, Saint Petersburg, and Novosibirsk. This happened in retaliation for Berlin's actions following an attempted drone attack at Leipzig airport in early August. In early September, German authorities blamed Moscow for the attack. They announced sanctions that included closing the Russian House culture and education center in Berlin. They also shut the Russian Consulate General in Bonn and tightened visa restrictions for Russian citizens. Goethe-Institut Secretary General, Gitte Zschoch, stated that all employees must cease their work by September thirteenth. This ends book loans, teacher training, and access to German language and culture programs. Goethe-Institut president, Gesche Joost, called the branch closures the end of an era in bilateral cultural relations. In twenty twenty-five, approximately ten thousand people studied German through the institute's programs and partnerships. This was down from about sixteen thousand before twenty twenty-three. The institute also administered roughly twenty-two thousand exams and recorded six thousand seven hundred library visitors last year.

item.title: Turkey: 162 arrested in LGBTQ+ raids
item.description: Turkish police arrested at least one hundred sixty-two people during weekend raids across fifteen provinces. Officers searched the offices of six L. G. B. T. Q. plus associations. Justice Minister, Akin Gurlek, stated that the operations involved judicial proceedings against one hundred sixty-two suspects and nine associations. Thirteen businesses were also targeted in the sweep. The actions were coordinated by prosecutors in Istanbul, Ankara, Izmir, Aydin, and Mersin. Authorities reported seizing drugs and digital equipment. Smuggled alcohol and a gun were also found. The operations targeted gay bars and night clubs along with a hammam. The Ankara-based rights group, Kaos G. L., claimed the government restricted access to dozens of websites. Social media accounts belonging to associate groups and advocates were also blocked. The raids were part of President, Recep Tayyip Erdogan, and his Decade of Family and Population scheme. The initiative is dubbed My Family is Safe. It aims at reversing declining birthrates in the country. President, Recep Tayyip Erdogan, has blamed L. G. B. T. Q. plus individuals for the fertility drop. Turkey's total fertility rate fell sharply from two point eleven in twenty thirteen. It dropped to one point five one in twenty twenty-three. Observers attribute the declining birthrate to structural issues. These include the financial crisis and high housing prices. Turkish Justice Minister, Akin Gurlek, added more details in a social media post. He cited the constitutional duty to protect families and children. He stated that no targeted illegal activity or abuse network would be tolerated. The Istanbul prosecutor's office reported finding evidence of a specific crime. Minors were allegedly being inappropriately swayed on sexual orientation and gender identity. Rights groups asserted that the government is unfairly targeting the community.

item.title: Scientists find a new layer of Alzheimer’s hidden in the genome
item.description:
Researchers from Carnegie Mellon University, the University of Pittsburgh, and the University of Washington published a study in Science on September thirteenth, twenty twenty-six. The study revealed that the three-dimensional organization of the genome is disrupted in brain cells affected by Alzheimer's disease.
The team examined postmortem prefrontal cortex tissue samples from individuals with and without Alzheimer's disease. They used a technique called G. A. G. E. dash seq, spatial transcriptomic maps, and a deep learning model named Hicformer.
The investigation showed that large sections of the genome normally organized into distinct active and inactive compartments become less sharply defined in Alzheimer's cells. The researchers call this pattern increased compartment mingling.
Affected cells displayed fewer interactions between nearby genome sections. They showed more contacts between distant regions and weaker interactions between genes and nearby regulatory elements. These structural shifts were linked to reduced gene activity in programs involving neurons and synapses. They also linked to alterations in metabolism and cellular stress responses along with senescence-related programs in microglia.
Alzheimer's disease cannot be understood one layer at a time. That quote came from Jian Ma, the Ray and Stephanie Lane Professor of Computational Biology who led the study.
Hansruedi Mathys, assistant professor of neurobiology at the University of Pittsburgh, noted that the findings establish higher-order chromatin alterations as part of the molecular pathology associated with the disease. The disease currently affects seven million Americans. The research was supported by grants from the National Institutes of Health.

item.title: Gravitational-wave analysis narrows the search for black hole impostors
item.description:
Researchers analyzed data from the gravitational wave event G. W. twenty-four ten eleven. The event happened in October twenty twenty-four. They narrowed the search for black hole impostors by measuring a specific spin property. The measurement looked at the primary object in the merger.
The event was detected by the LIGO Hanford detector in the United States and the Virgo detector in Italy. The event involved two compact objects. Their masses were about nineteen point six and five point nine solar masses. The primary object had a spin of approximately zero point seven eight. It also had a high signal to noise ratio of about thirty-six.
Researchers used a method proposed in seventeen. Wait. Nineteen seventeen. No. The text says twenty seventeen. Let me use twenty seventeen. Researchers used a method proposed in twenty seventeen. The method tests whether compact objects are truly black holes. Scientists from the University of Birmingham and other institutes did the work. They combined parameter estimation with numerical relativity simulations.
Their findings were published in Physical Review Letters. The primary object is consistent with a rotating Kerr black hole. The study rules out certain alternatives like rotating boson stars. The data does not completely eliminate other exotic objects. These objects must have a compactness greater than or equal to zero point two four.
Co-first author, N. V. Krishnendu, noted the work successfully moves past simple questions. It places quantitative constraints on specific alternatives. The findings currently apply only to this specific binary object. Future improvements to detectors will help. The fifth observing run and planned third generation facilities will provide enhanced sensitivity. They will also provide larger source populations to further test compact objects.

item.title: Antonelli wins as Norris loses out under virtual safety car
item.description: Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli won the Spanish Grand Prix at the new Madring circuit. McLaren pole-sitter Lando Norris lost a comfortable lead because of a badly timed virtual safety car. Norris had already passed the pit exit when the V. S. C. was called on lap fifteen following Lance Stroll breaking down. That allowed Antonelli and Red Bull second-place finisher Max Verstappen to pit and save time. The caution period ended before Norris could make it around again. A subsequent slow seven-second pit stop by McLaren dropped Norris down to fifth. He could only recover to finish third on a track where overtaking proved nearly impossible. Antonelli admitted his eighth win in fourteen races this year felt bittersweet. He stated it is good to win but it does not feel as good because Lando deserved to win. Norris took the setback in stride. He noted they will take it on the chin and that there could be more wins this year. The victory extends Antonelli championship lead to eighty-one points over teammate George Russell. Russell finished fifth on a confusing strategy. The victory also puts Antonelli one hundred one points clear of Ferrari driver, Lewis Hamilton. Hamilton retired early with brake failure. Ferrari driver, Charles Leclerc finished fourth after leading late on an alternative strategy. Liam Lawson took sixth for Red Bull. Franco Colapinto finished seventh for Alpine. Oscar Piastri took eighth for McLaren. Arvid Lindblad finished ninth for Racing Bulls. Nico Hulkenberg rounded out the top ten in tenth position for Audi.

item.title: Brics 2026: Xi listening, PM Modi warns against weaponisation of minerals, tech
item.description: Modi addressed leaders of the grouping and partner countries on the four pillars of India’s B. R. I. C. S. chairship. Those pillars are resilience, innovation, cooperation, and sustainability. The Prime Minister’s remarks mirrored global concerns about China’s near monopoly over critical minerals processing. His words also cut towards the West for its tendency to use technology as a means of political exclusion. The New Delhi Declaration was issued on Saturday. It emphasized the need to promote reliable, diversified, resilient, and just supply chains for critical minerals. This ensures benefit sharing and value addition in resource-rich countries. Modi stated that the weaponization of technology and critical minerals can hinder shared progress. He emphasized inclusivity in the adoption of technology to meet the needs of the Global South. Modi addressed resilience amid global conflicts, pandemics, climate disasters, and supply chain disruptions. He mentioned new initiatives such as the Integrated Early Warning System and the Logistics Supply Chain Cooperation Framework. Under innovation, he highlighted three major projects. They are the B. R. I. C. S. Incubator Network, the B. R. I. C. S. Startup Innovation Fund, and the B. R. I. C. S. Network on Digital Agriculture. These connect A. I., geospatial technology, and Digital Public Infrastructure to the real needs of farmers. To foster cooperation, Modi noted the launch of B. R. I. C. S. CONNECT and the B. R. I. C. S. M. S. M. E. Cooperation Portal. These connect small enterprises with knowledge, finance, and new markets. For sustainability, he mentioned the establishment of the B. R. I. C. S. Digital Centre of Excellence for Smart Grids and Energy Storage. This centre helps make clean energy systems more reliable, efficient, and accessible. Modi remarked that the confidence of Global South countries in B. R. I. C. S. has grown. Their voices are heard and solutions are developed together with them.

item.title: Russia hits Ukrainian train shortly after Boris Johnson and top European officials leave station
item.description:
A Russian drone struck a train engine near Yahodyn. The strike happened two kilometers from the Poland border. It occurred shortly after former U K. Prime Minister Boris Johnson and other European security officials passed through the area on a separate train. No casualties were reported. Passengers had been evacuated just fifteen minutes before the strike.
The officials were returning from the Yalta European Strategy conference in Kyiv. They included U K. national security adviser Jonathan Powell. They also included former C. I. A. chief David Petraeus.
Ukraine's state railway company Ukrzaliznytsia made a statement. They said the diplomatic train carrying the officials may have been the intended target. They noted it had departed early due to timetable changes prompted by strike threats.
Former Swedish Prime Minister Carl Bildt also attended the conference. He reported that passengers on his train were ordered to prepare for evacuation. Those passengers were then allowed to proceed safely to Poland's border station in Dorohusk.
Boris Johnson posted on X. He stated that Vladimir Putin's senseless attack highlights why allies must urgently provide air defences.
The strike comes amid an escalation of Russian attacks targeting Ukraine's transportation network. This network has suffered severe damage since air travel was suspended following the start of the full-scale invasion in twenty twenty-two.

item.title: Astronomers unmask a supernova impostor
item.description:
New research reveals that the distant star, A. T. twenty sixteen b. l. u., is not a dying star. It is a supernova impostor driven by interactions with a hidden binary companion. The star sits about twenty-nine million light-years away, which is about one hundred seventy trillion miles. The primary star is a luminous blue variable about thirty-three times as massive as our sun. Discovered in twelve, the star has erupted twenty-seven times in quasi-periodic bursts about every one hundred thirteen days.
Astronomer, Mojgan Aghakhanloo, led a research team at the University of Virginia. They used new X-ray observations alongside archival data to uncover the mechanism behind the outbursts. The findings are detailed in a forthcoming paper in The Astrophysical Journal. The paper is titled, A. T. twenty sixteen b. l. u. Accretion-Powered Outbursts in a Luminous Blue Variable and Compact Object Binary, and it is currently available on Arxiv dot org.
The research team coordinated with multiple telescopes and more than thirty amateur astronomers. They successfully scheduled observations during the star's peak outburst in March twenty twenty-six. This effort included a target of opportunity request that interrupted the schedule of the Chandra X-ray Observatory. Chandra detected an X-ray source during the predicted outburst. Inadvertent Chandra observations from two thousand one to two thousand two showed no X-rays. The measured luminosity and calculated mass accretion rate indicate that the outbursts are caused by intermittent accretion onto a compact object. That compact object is like a black hole or a neutron star.
The researchers conclude that A. T. twenty sixteen b. l. u. is the first known case of a luminous blue variable supernova impostor whose outbursts are driven by intermittent accretion onto a compact object. The system consists of a massive star and a compact companion, making it a high-mass X-ray binary. Mojgan Aghakhanloo stated that the study provides a front-row seat to seeing what the star does before it dies. Aghakhanloo has secured additional Chandra observing time to study more of them and determine whether others behave the same way. Studying these systems helps advance the understanding of massive stars, which forge and spread heavy elements out into space.

item.title: US Open tennis 2026 men’s final: Alexander Zverev v Ben Shelton – live
item.description: The men's final updates begin at one p.m. E.T. or six p.m. B.S.T. Arthur Ashe Stadium is preparing for a crowd full of famous faces. The twenty twenty-six US Open men's final features Alexander Zverev playing against Ben Shelton. Fans are wondering if American soccer star Trinity Rodman will be in attendance for boyfriend Ben Shelton's match as she has for all his previous rounds. We probably won't see her today. Her Washington Spirit team in the National Women's Soccer League is playing the Boston Legacy about five hours south in D.C. Shelton is facing a date with destiny. He shared his mindset heading into the matchup. He stated that they are not done yet and the job is not finished. He expressed excitement to show his best. Shelton noted that the tournament has been uncharted territory. It placed him in new positions where he has beaten opponents he had never beaten before.

item.title: NFL roundup: Bears and Panthers set scoring record; Bills beat Texans in thriller
item.description:
Caleb Williams threw for two hundred sixty-nine yards and two touchdowns. He also ran for sixty-five yards and two more scores. The Chicago Bears defeated the Carolina Panthers in the highest-scoring season opener in National Football League history.
Chicago and Carolina combined for ninety-six points. This surpassed the previous record of eighty-eight. That old record was set in twenty eighteen during a game where Tampa Bay beat New Orleans forty-eight to forty.
The Bears scored fifty-nine points. This set a franchise record for points in an opener. That record had stood since nineteen forty-eight when Chicago scored forty-five points against Green Bay at Wrigley Field.
The fifty-nine points also marked the most ever allowed by the Panthers in team history. D'Andre Swift signed a thirty-three point seven five million dollar contract extension earlier in the week. He contributed one hundred twenty-four rushing yards on eighteen carries with three touchdowns.
Meanwhile, Kyle Monangai recorded one hundred yards rushing. This included a sixty-one-yard touchdown burst.

item.title: Fable 5.1 Solves the Cyphral Distich, a 370-year-old cipher
item.description:
Claude Fable five point one has successfully solved Sir Thomas Urquhart’s Cyphral Distich. This is a sixty-four number cryptogram consisting of two lines of thirty-two numbers from the author's sixteen fifty-three work Logopandecteision.
Fable five point one also deciphered Urquhart’s larger two hundred eighty-five number Cyphral Octastick from The Jewel published in sixteen fifty-two.
Historical-cipher researcher, Klaus Schmeh, lists the distich among his top fifty unsolved encrypted messages. Fable five point one decoded it in forty-four minutes using one hundred seventy-six thousand tokens.
The author stated that it tried a few approaches, but was finally able to solve it with two central realizations. The simple deciphering rule used the book itself as the key by mapping numbers to word indexes.
The resulting plaintext of the distich reads. O God uphold King Charls the Second and make him the supreme ruler of this land.
The solution demonstrates that A. I. models can solve historical mysteries and archival puzzles previously bottlenecked by human attention.

item.title: Registration without a phone number on Signal will use zero-knowledge proofs
item.description: Zero-knowledge proofs protect privacy by verifying usernames without revealing their actual contents. Signal clients are designed to not trust the server and remain safe without checking server code, Hackernews reports. The Signal organization should clarify technical details regarding privacy if phone number unlinking happens. Unlinking phone numbers entirely could allow spammers to create infinitely many free accounts by registering, unlinking, and repeating. A cooldown period of one month may still be insufficient to prevent spammers and scammers effectively. As the analysis notes regarding usernames and verification, zero-knowledge proofs are not only the technology behind donation badges and backup payments, but also behind groups. They cannot tie you to a specific donation just like they cannot tie you to a specific group, ensuring high user confidentiality across all platform interactions without compromising core system architecture. Removing phone numbers on Signal could enable spammers to create infinite free accounts despite proposed cooldown periods.

item.title: Unvaccinated Pennsylvania woman died of measles complications, coroner says
item.description: A forty-year-old unvaccinated woman in Jefferson County, Pennsylvania, has died of complications from measles. Pennsylvania is experiencing an explosive measles outbreak with over six hundred seventy cases and one hundred twenty-four hospitalizations across thirty-seven counties. This fatality marks the third vaccine-preventable measles-linked death in the United States this year, and all of them have occurred in Pennsylvania. Prior to these deaths, Pennsylvania had not reported a measles death in thirty-five years. In a news release dated September twelfth, Jefferson County Coroner, Greg Furlong, said the death was a heartbreaking loss for the family and an unfortunate reminder that measles can be a serious and potentially life-threatening disease. A preliminary death certificate obtained by the New York Times indicated the woman had several chronic medical conditions, including chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and required supplemental oxygen at all times. The certificate listed the immediate cause of death as respiratory failure due to suspected measles. Furlong stated that the woman's measles case had not yet been confirmed by testing, but she was unvaccinated and known to have been exposed to someone with the virus, and she exhibited symptoms including a rash at the time of her death. The coroner's office is working with the state health department, which stated it is aware of the case but has not yet added the death to the official state outbreak tally.

item.title: Zverev turns US Open tears into triumph in transformational year
item.description:
Alexander Zverev defeated American Ben Shelton six-three, seven-six, five-seven, six-two at the US Open. This secured his second Grand Slam title in three months following his French Open victory in June.
Zverev played with intense focus in front of a twenty-four thousand strong crowd. He did not initially realize he had won the match. He walked back to the baseline to start the next point before his team told him it was over.
Zverev later said he was in the zone and did not hear any noise at all.
This victory marks a stark contrast to his devastating loss in the twenty-twenty US Open final. In that match, he threw away a two-set lead against Dominic Thiem.
The twenty-nine-year-old German now holds the French Open and US Open titles in the same year. His father and coach, Alexander senior, supported him from the sidelines. Zverev also paid tribute to his mother for her support following his childhood type one diabetes diagnosis.
The world number two trails Jannik Sinner by one thousand eight hundred ten points in the rankings. There are two Masters one thousand events and the A. T. P. Tour finals remaining in the season.
Zverev has previously faced legal scrutiny. This included a four hundred fifty thousand euro fine via a penalty order for bodily harm against an ex-partner in October twenty-three. He denied the charge and the case was discontinued in May twenty-four following a settlement without a verdict on guilt or innocence.
He also denied separate accusations of physical violence made by another former girlfriend in October twenty, which involved no legal proceedings.

item.title: No cities on the moon—there isn't enough water, scientists say
item.description:
A new study published in Frontiers in Space Technologies finds that plans for lunar cities face a major water shortage. Asteroid impacts created cold traps in polar craters that held water ice for about four billion years. Moon orbiting missions started in twenty thirteen and mapped an estimated one billion tons of water. This supply will not support large populations over the long term.
Consider a best case scenario with ninety-eight percent recycling efficiency matching current International Space Station technology. A lunar city of one million people would exhaust that one billion tons of water in just over a century. Today, best estimates suggest the moon has thirty times less water than that one billion ton figure. This shorter timeline means a moon village with one thousand people or a town with ten thousand people could survive for several centuries or more.
Power generation is possible using three gigawatt photovoltaic arrays placed on sunlit crater rims. Sustaining larger populations will require finding more water beneath the surface rubble. Other solutions include improving recycling, using vertical farming, or importing water from asteroids.

item.title: Indonesia searches for 129 people missing after ferry capsizes
item.description:
Indonesian authorities on Monday intensified the search for one hundred twenty-nine people still missing after the ferry Virgo Transport eight overturned in the Java Sea.
At least six passengers were killed in the disaster. One hundred eight people were rescued following the incident on Sunday.
The one hundred nineteen meter vessel was carrying two hundred forty-three people. This included two hundred thirteen passengers and thirty crew members. It also carried eighty-nine vehicles when it capsized in Masalembo waters about one hundred forty-eight kilometers from Banjarmasin.
The ship was traveling from Surabaya in East Java province to Banjarmasin on Borneo Island. The captain issued a distress call around two a.m. Sunday. He reported the ship was listing in rough seas with waves up to three meters before contact was lost.
Mohammad Syafii, the National Search and Rescue Agency chief, spoke about the rescue effort. Seventeen ships and aircraft carrying about six hundred twenty-two personnel from the military, police, and other agencies were deployed for the search. Authorities used specialized underwater teams and navy-operated drones as well.
We remain hopeful of finding more survivors, Syafii told a video briefing. Distraught relatives gathered at command centers in Banjarmasin and Surabaya to await news of unaccounted family members.
Ferries are a common method of travel across Indonesia's archipelago of more than seventeen thousand islands. Disasters occur regularly due in part to weak enforcement of safety standards.

item.title: Canada seeks 'unique alliance' with EU, Carney says
item.description: Canadian Prime Minister, Mark Carney, on Sunday denied that Canada is seeking membership in the European Union. Carney clarified his position after a Wall Street Journal report claimed he was exploring associate membership in the European Union. Carney said on Sunday that he is pursuing an unprecedented alliance with the European Union to reduce Canada's economic dependence on the United States amid an escalating trade war. Discussions for the new alliance are set to begin at an upcoming European Union and Canada summit in Montreal, aimed at building a much stronger and deeper economic and security partnership. Carney's remarks precede a trip to France this week, where he will become the first head of government to attend the State of the European Union address in Strasbourg before delivering his own speech at the European Parliament. Tobias Cremer, a European lawmaker from Germany, called the visit a tremendous symbol, noting that Canada possesses many resources Europe currently lacks, including energy, rare earths, and raw minerals. Canada has already become the first non-European Union nation to join the bloc's defense procurement program and is scheduled to join the Eurovision Song Contest in twenty twenty-seven.

item.title: US Kennedy Center faces bankruptcy, Washington Post reports
item.description:
The John F Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts in Washington faces imminent bankruptcy. It could close as soon as Tuesday according to a report published by The Washington Post on Sunday. The institution board of trustees is chaired by President Donald Trump. The trustees set out the assessment in a fifty-seven-page report ahead of a special meeting on Tuesday.
The trustees argued that putting the president name on the building facade could be the only way to avoid certain fiscal collapse. They stated that the center will not be able to pay employees or meet maintenance costs within a few weeks. Board members are recommending the main building be closed immediately due to costs.
The fifty-seven-page report outlines that the center collected about one hundred twenty-four million dollars of the projected two hundred twenty million dollars in budgeted revenue. This left a roughly twenty-three million dollar deficit despite substantial spending cuts this past fiscal year. A spokesperson for the center blamed the financial problems on financial mismanagement by previous leadership. The spokesperson said Trump name had attracted new donors. The Washington Post reported that Trump would help the institution if his involvement is acknowledged.
Trump installed himself as chairman shortly after beginning his second term last year. In December his hand-picked board voted to rename the venue the Trump-Kennedy Centre. A court later blocked the move. The takeover has triggered artist cancellations. It has also driven ticket sales to their lowest levels since the C. O. V. I. D. pandemic.

item.title: How did the first Ultimate Championship go?
item.description: Athletics just finished its inaugural Ultimate Championship in Budapest. The three-day event featured three successive sell-out crowds. It offered a record ten million dollar prize pot for the sport's biggest stars. World Athletics and president Lord Coe spent three years creating this bold undertaking. They wanted a season-ending pinnacle event to engage new and bigger audiences. Star names received major prize money for their efforts. The event featured a striking visual appearance. The infield was painted black. The horizontal jumps used a pink sandpit. Organizers added television enhancements like live win probabilities. Critics complained because several disciplines were omitted based on viewer metrics. Distance track events like the ten thousand meters were left out. All shot put and discus events were also excluded. Usain Bolt served as the event ambassador. The greatest sprinter in history called it a good first step. He believes it can change track and field for the better. Josh Kerr is a British fifteen hundred meters champion. He earned a significantly increased pay cheque at the event. He welcomes anything that can push the sport to be more entertaining. The biennial championship will return in twenty twenty-eight after the Olympics. Questions still remain about its long-term placement alongside the established Diamond League schedule.

item.title: Iran says it destroys U.S. advanced drone over Hormuz as Middle East conflict intensifies
item.description:
The Iranian military announced Monday that its new advanced aerospace defense system intercepted and destroyed an American manufactured M. Q. one drone over the Strait of Hormuz.
The drone was produced by General Atomics and historically operated by the United States Air Force and the C. I. A.
It was downed amid ongoing exchanges between Tehran and Washington in a war now in its seventh month.
Omani foreign minister, Badr Albusaidi, announced on Sunday that an upcoming meeting between Gulf countries and Iran has been postponed.
Trump suggested the United States could continue its campaign against Iran and keep the oil like Venezuela.
He noted that United States revenue from the Venezuela arrangement has paid for the war many times.
Trump said he expects the conflict with Iran to end this year, possibly after the November midterm elections.
He added that Tehran has been calling constantly for peace talks, a claim Iran has previously dismissed.
Energy markets reacted sharply to the intensifying conflict.
Oil prices surged past one hundred dollars a barrel for the first time since May on Monday.
This happened after Saudi Arabia closed a key East-West energy pipeline following damage from Iraqi drones.
United States West Texas Intermediate futures rose two point three percent to one hundred two dollars and thirty-nine cents per barrel.
At the same time, Brent crude climbed two point four percent to one hundred seven dollars and eleven cents a barrel.

item.title: Africa’s richest man aiming to make $23bn from continent’s biggest-ever IPO
item.description: Africa's richest person Aliko Dangote could add twenty-three billion dollars to his net worth during the flotation of Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals on the Nigerian exchange on Monday. Guardian World reports that the initial public offering requires a minimum subscription of just ten shares at five thousand two hundred fifty naira with the share purchase process finishing on thirteen October. If completely subscribed the refinery's value is expected to rise to about sixty-five trillion naira. The twenty billion dollar Dangote refinery on the outskirts of Lagos opened in January twenty twenty-four and made Nigeria a net exporter of refined fuel. Aliko Dangote framed the offering as an initial public offering for the people to draw in a broad mix of investors and help build wealth and grow the economy. Aliko Dangote stated at an initial public offering signing ceremony in Lagos on seven September that we must be bold and lead the change to develop our economies. Fellow Nigerian billionaire Tony Elumelu called the event a landmark moment for Nigeria and a huge milestone for Africa. The refinery offering on the Nigerian exchange could add twenty-three billion dollars to Aliko Dangote's net worth and boost local wealth.

item.title: Brain implant lets people with paralysis speak and gesture at the same time
item.description: A new brain implant enables people with paralysis to speak while gesturing like nodding or waving. These exchanges done via an avatar could help them communicate with more nuance. New Scientist reports that Samantha Brosler at the University of California, San Francisco, and her colleagues tested an I. Phone sized implant in two participants with paralysis. The first participant was named Bravo-one-r, who became paralyzed after a stroke. The second participant was named Bravo-six, who had amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. Both participants had lost almost all movement in their limbs and could only make unintelligible sounds. The team recorded brain activity while participants attempted to say ten phrases or perform ten gestures. They used this data to train customised machine learning models. Bravo-one-r's intended gestures and speech were predicted with eighty-eight and eighty-four percent accuracy. Bravo-six's were predicted with sixty-six and seventy percent accuracy. Samantha Brosler noted that if those models operated on complete chance, accuracy would be like nine percent. Henri Lorach at the University of Loh-zahn in Switzerland described it as a very nice piece of work with robust results. He noted it is based on a limited set of phrases and gestures that still need improving for daily use without frustration. The team is now working to address this by further training the models and tweaking the algorithms. The new implant technology could improve communication options for thousands of paralyzed patients globally through advanced machine learning models.

item.title: NASA Welcomes Djibouti as Newest Artemis Accords Signatory
item.description: The Republic of Djibouti officially became the seventy-second nation and eighth African country to sign the Artemis Accords. The ceremony took place on Monday at the National Aeronautics and Space Administration Headquarters in Washington, according to Nasa Breaking. Ambassador Mohamed Siad Douale signed the agreement for his country, while National Aeronautics and Space Administration Deputy Administrator Matt Anderson hosted the event. Djibouti launched its national space program in twenty twenty, and sent its first satellites into orbit using American rockets in twenty twenty-three and twenty twenty-four. United States State Department Assistant Secretary Frank Garcia also participated in the signing to promote peaceful space cooperation. Djibouti deepens its partnership with the United States and expands African participation in lunar exploration governance.

item.title: Athens Is Turning its Old Airport into One of Europe’s Largest Parks
item.description: A former Athens airport site is transforming into the Ellinikon Park. It will stretch over four hundred acres along the sea in a southern suburb, according to Good News Network. Planners designed the space to serve as a shaded refuge for residents of Europe is hottest city. The project aims to keep the park seven point two degrees Fahrenheit cooler than surrounding asphalt and concrete areas. To achieve this thermoregulation, the park will feature thirty thousand trees and three million smaller plants representing more than five hundred twenty species of flora. Rest areas will offer a shading ratio of more than sixty percent, while water features include running channels and misting systems. Athens previously held the World Meteorological Organization record for the highest temperature ever recorded in Europe at forty-eight point zero degrees Celsius. In twenty twenty-four, under the mayorship of Haris Doukas, the city began planting its first micro-forest alongside greening projects across six neighborhoods. The Ellinikon Park will utilize onsite water treatment facilities and a giant rainwater catchment system to support its flora. The park is planned to open to the public next year, with future renovations scheduled for twenty thirty. The urban cooling project sets a municipal climate adaptation precedent for dense southern European cities facing rising summer temperatures.

item.title: AI infrastructure company Cornelis raises $205M to chip away at Nvidia’s dominance
item.description: Artificial intelligence infrastructure company Cornelis announced on Monday that it has raised two hundred five million dollars in a funding round led by I. A. G. Capital Partners. Techcrunch reports that the company also unveiled a product named Active Compute Fabric. This network technology addresses the issue of graphical processing unit time wasted waiting for data by allowing chips to process and send information simultaneously. While Nvidia remains dominant and optimized for its own software stack, Cornelis is part of a new wave of infrastructure firms working to break that dominance chip by chip. Cornelis has already started shipping its current product and expects to release a new generation of the technology later this year, challenging Nvidia's market dominance by securing two hundred five million dollars to scale its new networking technology.

item.title: OpenAI buys smartphone camera maker Glass Imaging for $300 million, report says
item.description: OpenAI acquired smartphone camera maker Glass Imaging in a deal worth over three hundred million dollars, Techcrunch reports. Founded in twenty nineteen in Los Altos, California, Glass Imaging was created by former Apple engineers Ziv Attar and Tom Bishop. The startup had previously raised about thirty million dollars in funding from investors. Rather than editing photos after capture, Glass Imaging uses neural networks to overcome physical camera constraints and yield better images the moment the shutter clicks. The ChatGPT maker is rumored to be working on its own hardware devices like smartphones, earbuds, and A. I. companion devices. Previously in twenty twenty-five, OpenAI Chief Executive Officer Sam Altman and designer Jony Ive revealed they were working together on a device startup called io when OpenAI bought Ive company for six point five billion dollars. OpenAI did not immediately respond to a request for comment regarding the latest acquisition. The acquisition accelerates hardware development for the artificial intelligence company as it builds competing consumer devices.

item.title: ENISA launches Single Reporting Platform as EU Cyber Resilience Act vulnerability reporting obligations take effect
item.description: The E. U. Agency for Cybersecurity deployed the initial operating capability of the Single Reporting Platform. Tldr Infosec reports that the online tool was developed to enable manufacturers to meet their new Cyber Resilience Act reporting obligations for actively exploited vulnerabilities. The platform allows users to report once and communicate relevant information to all appropriate authorities. The framework supports a coordinated approach to vulnerability reporting across the European Union and builds a more resilient Digital Single Market. The new reporting platform standardizes vulnerability disclosures for European Union software manufacturers, altering compliance obligations across member states ahead of mandatory deadlines. From September eleventh twenty twenty-six, manufacturers are required to report actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe incidents having an impact on security. These obligations also apply to open source software stewards involved in developing products with digital elements. Main cybersecurity requirements apply from December eleventh twenty twenty-seven.

item.title: For the first time, the US military confirms it has deployed weapons in orbit
item.description: The United States has placed space control weapons in orbit, Air Force Secretary Troy Meink confirmed on Monday. Tldr Tech reports this is the first public declaration of the deployment, made during the Air and Space Forces Association annual conference near Washington, D. C. Meink declined to reveal specific details regarding the weapons or whether they have been tested. He noted that discussing such specifics would not benefit deterrence. Placing space control weapons in orbit provides the United States military with essential capabilities to defend joint forces against evolving adversary threats.

item.title: Elementic’s MO6 is the building material claiming to lock away carbon for thousands of years
item.description: A Finnish materials startup named Elementic created an innovative wall surfacing tile called M. O. six. Optimist Daily reports that the product is ninety percent carbon by chemistry and stores approximately two point four kilograms of atmospheric carbon dioxide for every kilogram of material used. Unlike traditional wood that eventually burns or decays, this material does not decay. Elementic general manager Johanna Normiala described the production method by stating we take the lignin, we create a kind of dough that we bake like a cake, and in the end we get a hard, resistant, durable material but which is lightweight. The company launched its debut collection named M. O. six Eternal on September second at the Habitare design trade fair in Helsinki as part of Helsinki Design Week. Elementic is intentionally positioning the product as a premium interior design brand to reach architects, hotel developers, and interior designers. A spa currently under construction in Paris is among the first named examples receiving the delivered product. The company expects further manufacturing improvements and plans to eventually develop bricks for broader construction applications. The permanent carbon storage product provides architects and developers a recyclable premium material that locks away emissions indefinitely.

item.title: Hyrox changes rules and apologises for allowing Australian athlete who soiled herself to continue
item.description: Fitness competition organisers have issued an apology and implemented immediate rule changes after an incident in Beijing. During the event, Guardian Sport reports that an Australian participant was allowed to finish and win despite soiling herself mid-race. Footage showed world record holder Joanna Wietrzyk continuing through demanding exercises and using communal equipment while visibly soiled. This sparked widespread debate regarding health and safety standards. Hyrox co-founder Moritz Fürste addressed the situation in an Instagram statement. He said that Hyrox made a mistake by failing to react immediately during the event and added that new procedures are now in place. Organisers from Hyrox China and Hyrox World confirmed that affected lanes were isolated for overnight deep cleaning. Contaminated equipment was removed, and venue carpets were replaced before competition resumed. The incident raised concerns among participants who paid to compete. Competitor Joe Ho noted that exposed athletes faced potential physical and psychological consequences and deserved meaningful compensation. Following online backlash targeting Wietrzyk, organisers issued a warning that individuals sending abuse or threats of violence toward the athlete will face bans from all future events. Fitness competition organisers face growing pressure to protect health standards and competitor welfare after hygiene failures during international racing events.

item.title: Alex Bores launches $30 million effort to unify Dems on AI
item.description: New York Assemblymember Alex Bores is launching a thirty million dollar effort called Who Decides to unite Democrats around regulating artificial intelligence. Bores is launching the new organization with his former chief of staff Anna Myers, Politico reports. The group aims by twenty twenty-eight to have Democratic candidates run with a common A. I. safety agenda. The agenda addresses current harms and broader dangers that increasingly powerful systems could destabilize the economy, democracy, and safety. The new political organization aims to unite Democrats around a common safety agenda to regulate frontier artificial intelligence by twenty twenty-eight. Who Decides will reject corporate money or contributions from senior executives at frontier A. I. companies. The initiative will conduct quarterly national and state polls, host national conferences, and partner with local groups in those states. The launch follows a failed congressional campaign earlier this year where Bores gained national attention for his opposition to unchecked artificial intelligence.

item.title: China tightens travel restrictions for citizens
item.description:
China has imposed sweeping new rules restricting travel in and out of the country to give the government more control over its citizens. Under the updated regulations, citizens who are deemed to have harmed national security or interests while overseas can be barred from leaving China for a period of up to three years. Bbc World reports that the law also applies to anyone considered a threat to the country's industrial or technological security. In March, the co-founders of an artificial intelligence company named Manus, which had been acquired by Meta, were reportedly barred from leaving China. Border officials are now required to advise Chinese nationals against traveling to countries and regions deemed high risk.
Official data highlights the scale of these measures. China's supreme court database showed only eighty-nine records mentioning exit bans in twenty-sixteen, but that figure surged dramatically to one hundred eighty-eight thousand seven hundred sixty last year. The percentage of civil verdicts that dealt with exit bans also surged more than thirty times between twenty-one and twenty-five, from around zero point two three percent to seven point three percent. Meanwhile, a Chinese government rumor refuting platform named Piyao posted a statement last week asserting that the new rules do not restrict ordinary citizens, but instead function as a preventative measure against high risk destinations and individuals with unusual travel patterns. However, Professor Tom Kellogg, Executive Director of the Center for Asian Law at Georgetown University, described the expanding travel restrictions as deeply concerning and stated that they reflect growing ideological control under Chinese leader Xi Jinping. The expanded travel restrictions increase operational risks for multinational technology companies relying on talent and research teams based inside China.

item.title: French labour strike reduces capacity at key Dunkirk gas terminal
item.description:
A twenty-four-hour labor strike on Tuesday reduced delivery capacity at the Dunkirk L. N. G. terminal to four gigawatt-hours per day. The terminal normally delivers a minimum of nine point four gigawatt-hours per day, France 24 Top reports using data from Fluxys. Industrial action was expected to reduce French electricity supply by up to five gigawatts on Tuesday, while taking six point five gigawatts offline overnight on Monday. Energy sector unions staged the strike to protest recommendations from the French Court of Auditors to curb employee benefits such as access to cheaper power. The labor strike restricts gas supply at Dunkirk while Europe scrambles to refill storage ahead of winter.
The disruption is likely to affect sendout ability only, as no cargoes were scheduled to arrive at Dunkirk, according to L. S. E. G. analyst Dzmitry Dauhalevich. Elengy confirmed no disruptions occurred at the Fos or Montoir terminals.

item.title: US Supreme Court rejects Trump’s plans on postal ballots: Why it matters
item.description:
The United States Supreme Court has rejected Donald Trump's bid to restrict voting by mail ahead of the November midterm elections. The ruling on Monday by the conservative supermajority court allows states to continue sending out mail ballots as they have done for years, according to Aljazeera.
In March twenty twenty-six, Trump signed an executive order directing the United States Postal Service to take control of mail voting. United States District Judge Indira Talwani imposed an injunction against the rule in June on the basis that it likely violated the United States Constitution. The Supreme Court refused to lift Judge Talwani's injunction in its latest and final decision, noting the administration was likely to fail. Justice Brett Kavanaugh voted with the majority against the administration, while Samuel Alito and Clarence Thomas dissented. The Supreme Court decision preserves mail voting procedures, protecting turnout as mail ballots account for a third of all votes cast. Mail ballots have been found to increase voter turnout. Critics have long warned that restricting mail-in ballots could disrupt the delivery of mailed votes as states have begun sending in midterm ballots. Eight states and the District of Columbia allow all elections to be conducted entirely by mail.

item.title: Air pollution spiked after the Trump administration stopped embassy monitoring
item.description: In March twenty twenty-five, the Trump administration shuttered the embassy air quality monitoring program citing monetary costs. Researchers reported Monday in the journal P. N. A. S. that air pollution levels increased by twenty-four to thirty-three percent over several months following the shutdown, Npr News reports. Eric Zou says that in two thousand and eight, US officials installed an air quality monitor on the embassy in Beijing and began making information public. Zoe Yiyuan Zhou and colleagues compared air pollution levels before and after monitoring ceased across forty-six cities using satellite data. Satellite measurements translate to about a four percent increase in P. M. two point five, which are small particles entering lungs and causing health problems. The pollution increase was highest in Southeast Asian cities including Manila in the Philippines, Rangoon in Myanmar and Vientiane in Laos. Andrea La Nauze stated that the program led to sustained improvements in air quality that were continuing to increase after ten years. Zoe Yiyuan Zhou stated that having access to information is necessary to make sure that these previous gains can continue. Public information creates accountability according to researchers studying the sudden falloff of surveillance. When industries find it costs money to cut down on pollution, companies may see a lack of monitoring as an opportunity to cut those costs. The State Department did not respond to a request for comment in time for publication regarding the shutdown of more than eighty embassy and consulate monitors. Ending embassy air quality monitoring increased pollution by up to thirty-three percent across foreign cities, raising health costs for local populations.

item.title: Japan considers boosting defense spending to 3.5% of GDP
item.description:
Japan is reportedly considering boosting its defense spending to three point five percent of gross domestic product. Semafor reports that the proposed defense spending increase responds to pressure from Washington amid rising East Asia tensions. The Trump administration has pushed Tokyo to reduce its support reliance, a move that has rattled policymakers and sparked worries about shifting United States commitments. Boosting defense spending to three point five percent of gross domestic product shifts Japan toward a more self-reliant security posture amid regional tensions.
Amid changing attitudes, voters in Okinawa recently ousted a governor who opposed Tokyo militarization. Seventy percent of the nation's United States military presence is located there. Some Japanese policymakers have begun to reconsider the country's long-standing ban on nuclear weapons. This military build-up and strategic shift aim to strengthen national security and respond directly to evolving geopolitical pressures across the region.

item.title: SCOTUS rejects Trump's mail voting limits. And, the Kennedy Center financial crisis
item.description: Senator Bernie Sanders and former strategist Steve Bannon joined forces at the Pro-Human Assembly in Washington, D. C., to address concerns about artificial intelligence. The Supreme Court blocked efforts to impose new mail-in voting restrictions before the midterm elections, ensuring the U. S. Postal Service will continue delivering ballots as usual, Npr News reports. Voting by mail has already started in states like Alabama, North Carolina, and Wisconsin. The Kennedy Center board says the arts institution faces bankruptcy and might close as soon as today, with a status hearing set by Judge Christopher Cooper overseeing a lawsuit from Representative Joyce Beatty seeking to halt the center renaming to honor Trump. Matthew Rhys pulled off a double play at the Emmys by winning lead actor in the limited series category for The Beast in Me and in the comedy series category for Widow's Bay, making him the first actor to ever win lead performance awards in two different categories in the same year. The Justice Department is investigating Evanston, Illinois, accusing it of racial discrimination over its reparations program. Costume and fashion designer Bob Mackie died of pneumonia in Palm Springs, California, on Monday at age eighty-seven. Mitch McConnell returned to the Senate yesterday after a months-long medical absence stemming from a fall. The administration is repealing limits on greenhouse gas emissions from fossil fuel-fired power plants, eliminating Environmental Protection Agency rules from the prior administration.

item.title: LSD could be approved for anxiety in the US in 2027
item.description:
Lysergic acid diethylamide could potentially gain U. S. Food and Drug Administration approval for treating anxiety as soon as twenty twenty-seven. This expectation follows a landmark clinical trial, according to New Scientist, showing that a single dose eased the mental health condition without severe or lasting side effects. Potential approval of the drug sets a regulatory precedent for psychiatric treatments in the United Kingdom and Europe.
Greg Cooper at University College London described the development as a milestone for psychiatric treatment. The trial recruited more than two hundred adults across the United States with moderate or severe generalised anxiety disorder. Participants assigned to take a one hundred microgram dose of the drug experienced a nine point eight point reduction in their anxiety levels after three months. That compares to a four point seven point drop in the placebo group. Robert Barrow at Definium Therapeutics noted that in a disorder with high unmet need, a single dose has shown a rapid and durable effect. Cooper emphasized that the results do not mean the drug is safe or effective to try at home. An episode can last for six to twelve hours and cause intense fear or panic. Participants were screened extremely carefully and given the drugs in a controlled environment. Unlike most psychedelic trials, participants were not offered ongoing psychotherapy, helping researchers isolate the drug-only effect.

item.title: Bangladesh court sentences 7 Hasina allies to death
item.description: A Bangladesh court on Tuesday sentenced seven senior allies of ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina to death in absentia. Dw Top reports the seven former Awami League officials were convicted of crimes against humanity for inciting killings during the twenty twenty-four protests. Prosecutor Mohammad Aminul Islam welcomed the verdict by saying most of the charges had been proven beyond reasonable doubt. The court also ordered the seizure of half of the defendants assets to provide compensation to families of victims. The United Nations estimates that as many as one thousand four hundred people were killed during the unrest in July and August twenty twenty-four. Sheikh Hasina was herself convicted of crimes against humanity in November twenty twenty-five and sentenced to death in absentia for her role in the crackdown. Tuesday verdict brings the total number of people convicted in trials connected with the twenty twenty-four uprising to sixty-eight. The death sentences and asset seizures for senior allies further destabilize the Awami League while the United Nations tracks accountability for the uprising.

item.title: Pidcock and Backstedt lead GB at Road Worlds
item.description:
Tom Pidcock and Zoe Backstedt will lead Great Britain at the twenty twenty-six Road World Championships in Montreal, Canada. Bbc Sport reports that the championships take place from September twentieth to September twenty-seventh and will be broadcast live across their platforms. Great Britain men have a strong chance to win because Tadej Pogacar is forced to sit out the rest of the season after suffering multiple injuries in a crash at the Vuelta a Espana. Ethan Hayter and Callum Thornley will compete in the men's time trial alongside defending champion Remco Evenepoel of Belgium. Zoe Backstedt steps up to the elite category after winning last year's Under-twenty-three race and joins Anna Henderson, who won silver in the time trial at the Paris Olympics in twenty twenty-four. British Cycling performance director Stephen Park said the Road World Championships are always one of the standout events in the cycling calendar and that this squad showcases the very best of British road racing. The absence of Tadej Pogacar improves Great Britain's medal prospects at the twenty twenty-six championships in Montreal.
The event includes road race and time trial disciplines with full coverage streaming on iPlayer and the Bbc Sport website and app throughout the week.

item.title: US admits to having weapons in orbit: How do they work, and should Russia, China worry?
item.description: The United States has acknowledged for the first time that it has weapons deployed in orbit, revealing a previously undisclosed military capability in space. United States Secretary of the Air Force Troy Meink stated on Monday, according to Livemint, that Washington possesses on-orbit space control weapons to protect American forces from hostile action. Meink made the disclosure during the Air and Space Forces Association conference held in Maryland. The decision to reveal the existence of the weapon was deliberate and intended to deter potential adversaries. He declined to discuss specific design details, capabilities, testing, or potential targets at a subsequent press roundtable. The United States Space Force later stated that space control missions involve both kinetic and non-kinetic methods aimed at challenging and controlling activity in orbit. Such capabilities could be used to disrupt, degrade, or destroy an adversary space system, serving both offensive and defensive purposes. Victoria Samson of the Secure World Foundation told the Financial Times that the weapon could be a space-based jammer. Clayton Swope of the Center for Strategic and International Studies noted that countries such as China and Russia are considered potential threats to American interests in space. In twenty twenty-five, President Donald Trump signed an executive order strengthening the Space Force responsibility for protecting American space assets and developing capabilities to attack adversaries systems. Satellites remain crucial for modern military operations, supporting communications, surveillance, and navigation in an increasingly contested orbital domain. The public acknowledgment of orbital weapons signals a major shift in military space policy, aimed at deterring adversaries and protecting critical satellite assets.

item.title: London loses bid to host 2029 World Athletics as Nairobi named host
item.description: London has missed out to Nairobi in the bid to host the twenty twenty-nine World Athletics Championships. Bbc Sport reports that an African city will host the event for the first time in history. The decision was confirmed at a World Athletics council meeting in Budapest where Munich was also confirmed as the host for the twenty thirty-one event. World Athletics president Sebastian Coe stated that Nairobi had presented a compelling and emotional bid. London missed out on the twenty twenty-nine hosting rights despite securing forty-five million pounds in public money and proposing the London Stadium as the host venue through a bid led by Athletic Ventures. Jack Buckner stated that U. K. Athletics was deeply disappointed that the championships will not be held in London and that they believed they had an outstanding bid which would genuinely take the sport to new levels. Amber Anning expressed disappointment that London missed out on hosting the event as a home competition while noting that having the championships in Africa for the first time will be really special. Taking the event to Africa fulfills the mission of growing athletics worldwide across Asia, Africa, and Europe over the next three editions while marking a historic milestone for the continent.

item.title: Robinhood To Offer Share Redemptions And Voting Rights On Tokenized Stocks
item.description: Online brokerage Robinhood Markets plans to offer share redemptions and voting rights on tokenized stocks. Chief Executive Officer Vlad Tenev announced the move in a social media post on September fourteenth. Yahoo Finance reports that the company is actively working on redemptions for shares one-to-one with voting for eligible token holders. Movie theatre chain A.M. C. Entertainment criticized Robinhood and called on the brokerage to stop offering a tokenized stock version. A.M.C. stated it has not approved the tokenized stock version and that token holders lack the rights of other shareholders. Providing in-kind redemptions allows investors to exchange a tokenized stock for a corresponding share. Voting rights help ease investor concerns and grant holders of tokenized stocks the same rights as other shareholders. Robinhood stock trades at one hundred fourteen dollars and thirty-three cents US per share and is down zero point four four percent over the last twelve months. Robinhood offering redemptions and voting rights on tokenized stocks addresses criticism from movie theatre chain A.M.C. Entertainment.

item.title: Merchants to now pay fees on UPI transactions above Rs 2,000 from Oct 15
item.description: The National Payments Corporation of India notified a merchant discount rate of zero point four percent on person-to-merchant U. P. I. transactions above two thousand rupees. The new rate becomes effective on October fifteenth, twenty twenty-six, according to Times Of India, giving acquiring banks and payment aggregators adequate time to update their software. Transactions of seventy-five thousand rupees and above will face a cap of three hundred rupees. Small-value payments up to two thousand rupees remain unaffected, while person-to-person transfers stay completely free. The new merchant discount rate provides predictable revenue for payment aggregators and banks while protecting small-value consumer transactions from fees. Finance Minister Nirmala Sith-a-ra-mun assured parliament that consumers will not pay fees for everyday payments, following amendments to the Payment and Settlement Systems Act of two thousand seven.

item.title: China, Russia warn against ‘weaponisation’ of space after US confirms orbital weapons
item.description: China and Russia warned against the militarisation of outer space on Tuesday after the United States confirmed it has weapons in orbit. Livemint reports that China urged the United States to stop expanding its military capabilities. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov called for international work toward complete demilitarisation. The warnings followed an acknowledgment by the United States Space Force that Washington possesses on-orbit space control weapons to defend forces. These capabilities include kinetic and non-kinetic means to affect adversary space systems. The American acknowledgment of orbital weapons risks accelerating an arms race and military competition in space with China and Russia.

item.title: Alappad panchayat in Keralam’s Kollam prepares for UNESCO Tsunami Ready status
item.description: A comprehensive mock drill was conducted on Tuesday across wards fourteen, fifteen, and sixteen. The exercise is part of preparations to secure tsunami ready recognition for Alappad grama panchayat in Kollam, according to The Hindu. The initiative is jointly implemented by the Intergovernmental Oceanographic Commission of the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization, along with national and state disaster management authorities. The exercise commenced at nine thirty a.m. when a tsunami alert was issued from the state authority to the district authority. Led by panchayat president, S. Jayasree, officials evacuated residents from the beach vicinity to a safe designated area near the Mukkumpuzha Devi temple. Vulnerable individuals received special attention from fire and rescue personnel and Aapda Mitra volunteers before evacuees were shifted to a relief camp at the Doctor V. V. Velukutty Arayan Government Regional Fisheries Technical High School supported by a medical team. The coastal security drill prepares local residents across three wards for tsunami emergencies ahead of international certification.

item.title: 10-year Treasury yield hits highest level since 2007 as traders bet a Fed rate hike is coming
item.description:
The bench marks ten-year Treasury yield climbed to five point zero four one percent on Tuesday, reaching its highest level since July two thousand and seven. The thirty-year Treasury bond yield rose to a high of five point four zero one percent, also hitting its highest level since June two thousand and seven.
Traders are pricing in a more than ninety-two percent chance that the Federal Reserve will raise rates by twenty-five basis points, Cnbc Top reports. U. S. ten-year treasuries are highly sensitive to inflation expectations. Jonathan Liang, Standard Chartered chief investment officer of fixed income and foreign exchange, stated that with inflation gauges still above the Federal Reserve target of two percent, this tight correlation will likely persist for a while. Higher Treasury yields increase borrowing costs for corporate funding and consumer loans across the broader economy.
West Texas Intermediate crude oil topped one hundred and two dollars a barrel on Tuesday as the Iran conflict drags on and the Strait of Hormuz remains essentially blocked. Meanwhile, National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett told C. N. B. C. on Tuesday that he believes inflation is showing signs of cooling based on near-term memory and the stochastic process that drives inflation.
